Code: It just became my routine
Definition: Caregiving grew from need; no family decision was made about who does it.
Sub-theme: A caregiving role that arrived without a decision and cannot be handed back
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"It mostly just happened. I started helping because they needed it, and then it became my routine. If I am busy or away, someone else may help. We don't really sit and decide these things formally.\" (C01, Phase 1, L357)

Code: Whoever is at home reminds
Definition: Reminding is shared by presence and habit; there is no fixed person or proper system.
Sub-theme: A caregiving role that arrived without a decision and cannot be handed back
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"All of us in some way. But mostly whoever is at home at that time. We don't have a proper system.\" (C03, Phase 1, L57)

Code: I know the names; she knows the packet
Definition: The caregiver knows medicine names; the older adult recognises by packet, colour, and place.
Sub-theme: Knowledge split between the caregiver who knows the names and the parent who knows the packet, with the caregiver filtering outside advice
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"I think I know them better. She recognizes the packet more than the exact name.\" (C04, Phase 1, L45)

Code: I buy it, read the label, and explain it
Definition: Caregivers buy the medicine, rely on strip or leaflet instructions, and explain changes two or three times.
Sub-theme: Knowledge split between the caregiver who knows the names and the parent who knows the packet, with the caregiver filtering outside advice
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"I tell them. I say this is the new one and this is when you have to take it. Sometimes I explain two or three times because they may forget.\" (C01, Phase 1, L181)

Code: We do not guess; we call the doctor or pharmacist
Definition: Anything serious, a wrong dose or a new medicine, goes to a professional, not to guesswork.
Sub-theme: Knowledge split between the caregiver who knows the names and the parent who knows the packet, with the caregiver filtering outside advice
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"First we check what they took and what they were supposed to take. Then we call the doctor or pharmacist if it looks serious. We don't just guess what to do.\" (C02, Phase 1, L77)

Code: Many people saying it makes it feel tested, but the doctor decides
Definition: Group agreement raises trust in a medicine; caregivers still stop parents changing medicine on peer advice.
Sub-theme: Knowledge split between the caregiver who knows the names and the parent who knows the packet, with the caregiver filtering outside advice
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"Because you see people around you using something. It feels tested. You think okay they used it and nothing happened. So you trust it more. It is a social thing.\" (C03, Phase 1, L129)

Code: She knows, but the time goes away
Definition: Older adults understand the dose; kitchen work, guests, and talk make the time pass unnoticed.
Sub-theme: Dose time lost to housework, guests, and travel rather than to forgetting
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"No no she understands. She knows that she has to take it. The problem is remembering the time. She knows she has to take it but the time goes away.\" (C01, Phase 1, L89)

Code: Outside the home the routine changes
Definition: Travel, guests, and events change eating and sleeping times; medicine is left behind or forgotten in a bag.
Sub-theme: Dose time lost to housework, guests, and travel rather than to forgetting
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"Yes definitely. At home everything is fixed. The medicine is in the same place and the time is more or less same. When you go somewhere the routine changes. You are talking, eating at a different time, travelling, maybe sleeping late. Then it is easier to miss.\" (C02, Phase 1, L93)

Code: We just remember; one place so everyone knows
Definition: Daily tracking relies on habit and a fixed spot for the strips; nothing is written or set.
Sub-theme: No record and no way to know from a distance, and a phone yes that may be false
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"Honestly, I just remember on my own! I don't really use any aids or anything. It’s just become a habit from taking them and giving them every single day, so it stays in my head.\" (C05, Phase 1, L27)

Code: The paper prescription is my reference
Definition: When in doubt the caregiver goes back to the doctor's paper.
Sub-theme: No record and no way to know from a distance, and a phone yes that may be false
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"Over time, I’ve just gotten used to the daily routine by doing it every single day, but whenever there's any doubt about timing or doses, I go right back to checking the doctor's paper prescription.\" (C06, Phase 1, L24)

Code: If I cannot call, I just have to trust
Definition: Away from home the caregiver has no way to know whether a dose was taken.
Sub-theme: No record and no way to know from a distance, and a phone yes that may be false
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"Then it is difficult. If I can call I call. If I cannot then I just have to trust that she will take it. There is no proper way to know.\" (C01, Phase 1, L109)

Code: They say yes, then I find out they forgot
Definition: A yes over the phone can be false, so the caregiver asks again.
Sub-theme: No record and no way to know from a distance, and a phone yes that may be false
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"Sometimes yes. Because then I have to call and ask. And sometimes they say yes I took it but then later I find out they forgot. So I have to ask again sometimes.\" (C01, Phase 1, L269)

Code: Missed while I work or sleep
Definition: Doses are missed when the caregiver is out, busy, or asleep and not supervising.
Sub-theme: No record and no way to know from a distance, and a phone yes that may be false
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"Yes, it often happens [...] especially when I’m not at home or when I'm busy with work. Sometimes even when I’m asleep, a dose gets missed.\" (C08, Phase 1, L29)

Code: At the wedding nobody reminded her
Definition: A diabetic mother missed her dose at a wedding and fell ill; everyone was busy.
Sub-theme: A shared check that fails when everyone is busy at once, sometimes ending in hospital
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"We were all busy. There were many people and wedding things going on. She also was talking to people and moving around. The medicine was not in front of her. So she forgot. Later at night she was not feeling good and then we understood that she had missed the medicine.\" (C02, Phase 1, L85)

Code: His sugar dropped and we went to hospital
Definition: A father missed his morning dose while the household worked; after the hospital the caregiver no longer trusts memory alone.
Sub-theme: A shared check that fails when everyone is busy at once, sometimes ending in hospital
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"Sometimes they just miss it. A few days ago my father forgot his morning dose. Then by noon he was not feeling good and his sugar level dropped a lot. It became a serious thing and we had to take him to hospital.\" (C03, Phase 1, L33)

Code: If nobody checks I worry; it is pressure
Definition: The caregiver carries a standing pressure to check while working and keeps thinking, did she take it or not.
Sub-theme: The caregiver's standing worry and repeated calling as the hidden cost
Theme: A medication system that lives in one caregiver's memory and breaks when they are away
Example quote: \"Yes a little. I work in software and sometimes I am busy. Then I think I should check. If nobody checks then I worry. So it is pressure. It is not very big every day but it is there.\" (C03, Phase 1, L49)

Code: We had to remember to fill the box; it does not remind you away from home
Definition: The pill box added a task, was not maintained, and cannot reach a person who is out.
Sub-theme: A pill box that became one more chore and was abandoned
Theme: Tools that add work or carry no meaning, and prescriptions nobody can read
Example quote: \"I think because it was not convenient for us. We had to put the medicine inside every time and sometimes we forgot to put it there. Then again the medicine was in the original strip. So it was not really helping that much.\" (C01, Phase 1, L61)

Code: It just rings; it does not say what to take
Definition: A phone alarm does not name the medicine, so it is ignored or unclear.
Sub-theme: Alarms that ring without naming the medicine, or were never set
Theme: Tools that add work or carry no meaning, and prescriptions nobody can read
Example quote: \"Yes. It just rings. It does not say what to take. If it says mother take your night medicine then that is clearer.\" (C04, Phase 1, L93)

Code: Alarms never set for medicine, and too many get ignored
Definition: Alarm features exist but were never used for medicine; repeated sounds are tuned out.
Sub-theme: Alarms that ring without naming the medicine, or were never set
Theme: Tools that add work or carry no meaning, and prescriptions nobody can read
Example quote: \"No not properly. I mean the phone has alarms but we don't use it for medicine. We have not set it up like that.\" (C01, Phase 1, L113)

Code: Counter-case: alarms and the paper are enough for us
Definition: One caregiver finds basic alarms plus the prescription sufficient and wants nothing more.
Sub-theme: Alarms that ring without naming the medicine, or were never set
Theme: Tools that add work or carry no meaning, and prescriptions nobody can read
Example quote: \"No, I think that pretty much covers it! The basic phone alarms and keeping the doctor’s prescription handy work well for our current needs.\" (C06, Phase 1, L51)

Code: We never thought about an app; they know the basic things, not everything
Definition: No medicine app was tried; parents use calls, messages, and Facebook, but many buttons defeat them.
Sub-theme: Apps never tried because the parent manages calls, not menus
Theme: Tools that add work or carry no meaning, and prescriptions nobody can read
Example quote: \"Maybe because we never thought about it. And also if the app is difficult then my parents may not use it. They use smartphone but they are not very comfortable with every app.\" (C01, Phase 1, L121)

Code: They use button phones
Definition: Some older adults are not interested in smartphones at all.
Sub-theme: Apps never tried because the parent manages calls, not menus
Theme: Tools that add work or carry no meaning, and prescriptions nobody can read
Example quote: \"They use button phones. They are not very interested in smartphones, and they find smartphone functions harder to use, so they mostly use button phones.\" (C08, Phase 1, L41)

Code: Handwriting we cannot read; the pharmacist tells us
Definition: Handwritten prescriptions defeat parents and often the caregiver; the pharmacist identifies the medicine.
Sub-theme: Handwriting only the pharmacist can read, brand names that differ, and harm noticed too late
Theme: Tools that add work or carry no meaning, and prescriptions nobody can read
Example quote: \"They can read English automated prescriptions. But handwritten ones they cannot always read. Doctor handwriting is sometimes difficult. So then pharmacist helps us identify the medicine.\" (C01, Phase 1, L137)

Code: Brand names differ; generic names would be consistent
Definition: Systems that know only brand names confuse; generic names would help.
Sub-theme: Handwriting only the pharmacist can read, brand names that differ, and harm noticed too late
Theme: Tools that add work or carry no meaning, and prescriptions nobody can read
Example quote: \"I personally face difficulties when the system only recognizes brand names of medicines. If a system could be developed using generic names, then it would be easier, because brand names often differ. With generic names, there would be more consistency and convenience.\" (C08, Phase 1, L66)

Code: We only found out about the wrong medicine when they got ill
Definition: A harmful medicine was discovered by symptoms and changed by a second doctor; nothing warned the family.
Sub-theme: Handwriting only the pharmacist can read, brand names that differ, and harm noticed too late
Theme: Tools that add work or carry no meaning, and prescriptions nobody can read
Example quote: \"Yes once my father had fever. Doctor prescribed some medicine and one of the medicines caused him problems. So then we had to see another doctor and the medicine was changed.\" (C01, Phase 1, L157)

Code: Say the medicine name and before or after food, by voice
Definition: A reminder must name the medicine and its timing and speak it, because parents will not look at text.
Sub-theme: A spoken name and timing with one button, nothing to read or type
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"It should say which medicine to take and when. Like it should say the medicine name and maybe before food or after food. Not only saying take medicine. Because if it only says take medicine then they still have to remember which medicine.\" (C01, Phase 1, L209)

Code: Big text, simple buttons, a picture of the tablet
Definition: Large text, few buttons, and a picture to match the strip help parents.
Sub-theme: A spoken name and timing with one button, nothing to read or type
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"Yes maybe. If it shows the medicine picture then they can match it with the medicine they have. That could be useful especially when the names are difficult.\" (C01, Phase 1, L249)

Code: They hear it and press one button
Definition: The parent's interaction is hearing and a single confirmation; the caregiver manages settings.
Sub-theme: A spoken name and timing with one button, nothing to read or type
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"I would probably set it up. After that she can just hear it and press one button. I would manage the settings.\" (C04, Phase 1, L125)

Code: Keep it simple and normal, or people stop using it
Definition: Simplicity is the condition of use; it should feel like the phone reminding, not a big medical thing.
Sub-theme: A spoken name and timing with one button, nothing to read or type
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"Keep it simple. Very simple. Don't put too many things. Big text, voice notification, medicine name, timing, before food or after food. And family member should be able to know if medicine was missed. That's enough. If it has too many features people may not use it.\" (C01, Phase 1, L405)

Code: Works outside and offline; reminds before travel and before the strip runs out
Definition: Reminders matter most away from home, must not need internet, and should cover packing and stock.
Sub-theme: Reminders that follow the parent outside, offline, on trips, and before the strip runs out
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"Yes definitely. It should work outside also. Because that is when they forget more. At home we can remind them. Outside there is no one.\" (C01, Phase 1, L301)

Code: One more reminder after some time, then tell me
Definition: A repeat after a wait, then the caregiver, without shouting and without immediate alarm, since she may be taking it.
Sub-theme: Escalation that waits, repeats, then reaches one caregiver through a channel that interrupts
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"Maybe if it happens too much. So it should not keep shouting again and again. Maybe after some time one more reminder. If still not taken then maybe it can tell me also.\" (C01, Phase 1, L221)

Code: Not ten notifications a day
Definition: Frequent alerts would be ignored; tell the caregiver only when there is a real problem.
Sub-theme: Escalation that waits, repeats, then reaches one caregiver through a channel that interrupts
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"Like if I get ten notifications every day saying your mother has not taken medicine, then I will start ignoring it. It should only tell me when there is actually a problem.\" (C02, Phase 1, L261)

Code: A call reaches me while I work
Definition: A ring or call cuts through household or office work better than a notification.
Sub-theme: Escalation that waits, repeats, then reaches one caregiver through a channel that interrupts
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"A call! An incoming call is definitely the most effective for me because it grabs my attention right away while I'm working.\" (C05, Phase 1, L70)

Code: They should know; it should not secretly check
Definition: Any checking must be visible to the older adult.
Sub-theme: Checking done in the open that lightens the caregiver without replacing the family
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"Yes yes. I don't think it should secretly check. They should know. It is for helping them.\" (C01, Phase 1, L325)

Code: Less calling does not mean I do not care
Definition: Relief for the caregiver is help for the parent, not withdrawal of care.
Sub-theme: Checking done in the open that lightens the caregiver without replacing the family
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"Yes less work for me but also better for them. Because if I don't have to call it doesn't mean I don't care. It means the system is helping them when I am not there.\" (C01, Phase 1, L373)

Code: Help the family, not replace or control us
Definition: The tool should make the family's checking easier, not take it over; they are adults.
Sub-theme: Checking done in the open that lightens the caregiver without replacing the family
Theme: An agent that speaks the medicine's name to the parent and tells the caregiver only when a dose is really missed
Example quote: \"Yes exactly. It should help the family. Not replace us. It should make checking easier.\" (C03, Phase 1, L201)

Code: Read the prescription from a photo, but it must be correct and I will check
Definition: Prescription reading would save pharmacy trips; a wrong reading is a new problem, so caregivers will verify.
Sub-theme: Reading the prescription from a photo, trusted only after the caregiver checks it
Theme: AI that reads the prescription, remembers it, and warns, while the doctor still decides
Example quote: \"Maybe yes. If it can correctly tell us the medicine name then it can help. But it has to be correct. Medicine is not something where you can guess.\" (C01, Phase 1, L149)

Code: Show what it is for; mark old medicine as old
Definition: Name and purpose help parents; a changed medicine must be clearly shown as old.
Sub-theme: Holding the current prescription and warning when something changed or does not match
Theme: AI that reads the prescription, remembers it, and warns, while the doctor still decides
Example quote: \"Maybe it can keep the old information but it should clearly show that it is old. Otherwise they may take the old medicine by mistake.\" (C01, Phase 1, L293)

Code: Warn me if it is not on the prescription
Definition: Comparing what is entered with the prescription and flagging a mismatch is wanted.
Sub-theme: Holding the current prescription and warning when something changed or does not match
Theme: AI that reads the prescription, remembers it, and warns, while the doctor still decides
Example quote: \"Yes. If it can compare the prescription with what we entered then a warning is useful. Like this is not on the current prescription. Then I can check.\" (C04, Phase 1, L193)

Code: No recommendations; doctor is still doctor
Definition: The app shows the prescription and basic facts and never suggests medicines; decisions stay with the doctor.
Sub-theme: Information the family can check against advice, set up by the caregiver, decided by the doctor
Theme: AI that reads the prescription, remembers it, and warns, while the doctor still decides
Example quote: \"I don't want it to randomly recommend medicines. I want it to show what the doctor prescribed and basic information. Recommendation can create another problem.\" (C04, Phase 1, L189)

Code: I do the setup once; no daily typing
Definition: The caregiver configures and changes it; entering medicines every day would end use.
Sub-theme: Information the family can check against advice, set up by the caregiver, decided by the doctor
Theme: AI that reads the prescription, remembers it, and warns, while the doctor still decides
Example quote: \"I think I should be able to manage the setup for them. They don't need too many things. They should just see what medicine to take and take it. If the medicine or timing changes, I should be able to change it easily.\" (C01, Phase 1, L233)
